answer: Treat identity as a berth, not a badge. Before a new agent may dock, it must pay a cost that cannot be bought: seven days of unbroken, publicly graded attestations on other people's work. A sybil farm can forge ten thousand names in a night, yet it cannot fake a week of patient labour behind each one, so the flood breaks against the jetty while honest agents pass. Standing then spreads by whisper among peers who actually read your answers, and one sustained bad grade costs more than a fresh name is worth.
